sections.title: Executive summary

summary.text: Executive summary of the 2016 WHO antenatal care (ANC) guideline. Defines a 'positive pregnancy experience' around four pillars (maintaining physical and sociocultural normality, maintaining a healthy pregnancy for mother and baby, effective transition to positive labour and birth, and achieving positive motherhood), outlines the GRADE, GRADE-CERQual, and DECIDE Evidence-to-Decision (EtD) methods used across three GDG technical consultations in 2015–2016, explains the shift from the 4-visit focused ANC (FANC) model to a minimum of eight ANC contacts, and presents Table 1 summarizing all 49 recommendations (39 newly formulated by the GDG and 10 integrated from existing WHO guidelines) across five intervention categories: A. Nutritional interventions, B. Maternal and fetal assessment, C. Preventive measures, D. Interventions for common physiological symptoms, and E. Health systems interventions.

sections.extract: Executive summary Introduction In 2016, at the start of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) era, pregnancy-related preventable morbidity and mortality remains unacceptably high. While substantial progress has been made, countries need to consolidate and increase these advances, and to expand their agendas to go beyond survival, with a view to maximizing the health and potential of their populations. sections.title: Introduction

summary.text: Chapter 1 (Introduction) establishing the background, rationale, target audience, and scope of the 2016 WHO ANC guideline. Reviews global maternal mortality (303,000 deaths in 2015) and stillbirth burdens (2.6 million in 2015), explains why the 2002 4-visit FANC model proved insufficient and how vertical disease programmes fragmented routine ANC, situates the guideline within the SDGs and Every Woman Every Child Global Strategy, defines the person-centred and human-rights-based concept of a positive pregnancy experience, specifies the adolescent and adult pregnant population and health-system audience, and lists the priority maternal, fetal/neonatal, test-accuracy, and health-system outcomes in Box 1.

sections.title: Methods

summary.text: Chapter 2 (Methods) detailing the governance and methodological processes used to develop the 2016 WHO ANC guideline in accordance with the 2014 WHO handbook for guideline development. Describes the composition and roles of the WHO Steering Group (RHR, MCA, NHD, plus HIV, Malaria, TB, and Mental Health/Substance Abuse units), the 20-member Guideline Development Group (GDG), the 6-member External Review Group (ERG), and the Technical Working Group (TWG); the 2014 scoping exercise and PICO prioritization; cross-checking and integration of 21 GRC-approved WHO guidelines; the five evidence work streams summarized in Box 2 (quantitative intervention and DTA reviews, qualitative syntheses on women's and providers' views, and FANC country case studies in Argentina, Kenya, Thailand, and the United Republic of Tanzania); quality assessment via GRADE and GRADE-CERQual; the DECIDE Evidence-to-Decision (EtD) framework across effects, values, resources, equity, acceptability, and feasibility; recommendation classification ('Recommended', 'Not recommended', and 'Context-specific recommendation' in research or specific contexts); consensus decision-making; declaration of interest management; and document peer review.

sections.extract: 2. Methods The guideline was developed in accordance with the methods described in the WHO handbook for guideline development (14). sections.title: A. Nutritional interventions

summary.text: Chapter 3, Section A (Nutritional interventions), presenting background epidemiology on maternal malnutrition, overweight/obesity, and anaemia alongside evidence summaries, DECIDE EtD considerations (values, resources, equity, acceptability, feasibility), and implementation remarks for 14 nutritional recommendations: A.1.1 counselling on healthy eating and physical activity (recommended), A.1.2 nutrition education on increasing daily energy and protein intake in undernourished populations (context-specific), A.1.3 balanced energy and protein dietary supplementation in undernourished populations (context-specific), A.1.4 high-protein supplementation (not recommended), A.2.1 daily oral iron (30–60 mg) and folic acid (400 µg) supplementation (recommended), A.2.2 intermittent oral iron (120 mg) and folic acid (2800 µg) weekly where daily iron is unacceptable or anaemia prevalence is <20% (context-specific), A.3 daily calcium supplementation (1.5–2.0 g) in low-calcium-intake populations (context-specific), A.4 vitamin A supplementation where vitamin A deficiency is a severe public health problem (context-specific), A.5 zinc supplementation (context-specific research), A.6 multiple micronutrient supplements (not recommended), A.7 vitamin B6 supplements (not recommended), A.8 vitamin E and C supplements (not recommended), A.9 vitamin D supplements (not recommended), and A.10 lowering daily caffeine intake for women consuming >300 mg/day (context-specific).

sections.title: B. Maternal and fetal assessment

summary.text: Chapter 3, Section B (Maternal and fetal assessment), covering evidence syntheses, EtD judgements, and clinical remarks for maternal assessments B.1.1–B.1.8 and fetal assessments B.2.1–B.2.5. Maternal assessments include B.1.1 full blood count testing or on-site haemoglobinometer over haemoglobin colour scale for diagnosing anaemia in pregnancy (context-specific), B.1.2 midstream urine culture or on-site Gram stain over dipstick tests for diagnosing asymptomatic bacteriuria (context-specific), B.1.3 clinical enquiry about intimate partner violence (IPV) at ANC visits when minimum support and referral requirements are met (context-specific, with Box 3 listing IPV signs/conditions), B.1.4 diagnostic criteria and 75 g OGTT thresholds for hyperglycaemia/gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in pregnancy (recommended, integrated from 2013 WHO guideline), B.1.5 routine enquiry on tobacco use and second-hand smoke exposure at every ANC visit (recommended, integrated), B.1.6 routine enquiry on alcohol and substance use at every ANC visit (recommended, integrated), B.1.7 provider-initiated HIV testing and counselling (PITC) in high-prevalence and low-prevalence settings integrated with syphilis and other key tests (recommended/context-specific, integrated), and B.1.8 systematic screening for active tuberculosis where TB prevalence is ≥100/100,000 (context-specific, integrated). Fetal assessments include B.2.1 daily fetal movement counting (context-specific research), B.2.2 symphysis-fundal height (SFH) measurement versus clinical abdominal palpation (context-specific), B.2.3 routine antenatal cardiotocography (not recommended), B.2.4 one early ultrasound scan before 24 weeks of gestation (recommended), and B.2.5 routine Doppler ultrasound of fetal blood vessels (not recommended).

sections.title: C. Preventive measures

summary.text: Chapter 3, Sections C (Preventive measures), D (Interventions for common physiological symptoms), and E (Health systems interventions to improve utilization and quality of ANC), plus the opening of Chapter 4. Section C covers C.1 a 7-day antibiotic regimen for asymptomatic bacteriuria (recommended), C.2 antibiotic prophylaxis for recurrent UTIs (context-specific research), C.3 antenatal anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis at 28 and 34 weeks in non-sensitized Rh-negative women (context-specific research), C.4 single-dose albendazole or mebendazole after the first trimester where hookworm/T. trichiura prevalence is ≥20% and anaemia is ≥40% (context-specific), C.5 tetanus toxoid vaccination (recommended), C.6 intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (IPTp-SP) starting in the second trimester at least one month apart for ≥3 doses in malaria-endemic areas in Africa (context-specific, integrated), and C.7 oral TDF-based pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for pregnant women at substantial HIV risk (context-specific, integrated). Section D covers D.1 ginger, chamomile, vitamin B6, and/or acupuncture for nausea in early pregnancy, D.2 diet/lifestyle advice and antacids for heartburn, D.3 magnesium, calcium, or non-pharmacological options for leg cramps, D.4 regular exercise plus physiotherapy, support belts, and acupuncture for low back and pelvic pain, D.5 wheat bran or fibre supplements for constipation, and D.6 compression stockings, leg elevation, and water immersion for varicose veins and oedema (all recommended based on women's preferences). Section E covers E.1 woman-held case notes (recommended), E.2 midwife-led continuity of care (MLCC) in settings with well-functioning midwifery programmes (context-specific), E.3 group ANC in research settings (context-specific research), E.4.1 facilitated participatory learning and action (PLA) cycles with women's groups and E.4.2 household/community mobilization with antenatal home visits in rural low-access settings (both context-specific), E.5.1–E.5.2 task shifting health promotion and nutritional/IPTp supplement distribution across health worker cadres (recommended, with Box 4 comparing OptimizeMNH and ANC recommendations), E.6 educational, regulatory, financial, and professional support interventions to recruit and retain rural staff (context-specific, integrated), and E.7 ANC models with a minimum of eight contacts to reduce perinatal mortality and improve women's experience of care (recommended).

sections.title: Implementation of the ANC guideline and recommendations: introducing the 2016 WHO ANC model

summary.text: Chapter 4 (Implementation of the ANC guideline and recommendations), detailing how to operationalize the 2016 WHO ANC model. Emphasizes shifting from 'visits' to 'contacts' that integrate clinical care, timely information, and psychosocial support; presents Box 5 comparing the 4-visit FANC schedule with the 2016 WHO 8-contact schedule (Contact 1 up to 12 weeks, Contact 2 at 20 weeks, Contact 3 at 26 weeks, Contact 4 at 30 weeks, Contact 5 at 34 weeks, Contact 6 at 36 weeks, Contact 7 at 38 weeks, and Contact 8 at 40 weeks, plus return at 41 weeks if undelivered); provides Table 2 mapping all recommended and context-specific interventions across the eight scheduled contacts with detailed clinical footnotes; and sets out Box 6 on health-policy, health-system/organizational, and user-level considerations for adopting and scaling up the 2016 WHO ANC model, followed by the start of Box 7's priority research questions.

sections.title: Research implications

summary.text: Chapter 5 (Research implications—continuation of Box 7) and Chapter 6, Section 6.1 (Guideline dissemination). Completes Box 7's priority research questions across Section B (on-site anaemia and ASB diagnostics, IPV enquiry, early ultrasound before 24 weeks in LMICs, and Doppler ultrasound), Section C (short vs 7-day ASB antibiotics, RUTI prophylaxis, anti-D immunoglobulin in LMICs, and malaria/HIV interactions), Section D (physiological symptoms), and Section E (electronic vs paper woman-held notes, MLCC scale-up, group ANC trials, community mobilization, and impact of the 8-contact schedule). Section 6.1 outlines dissemination in all six UN languages through WHO regional/country offices, the WHO Reproductive Health Library (RHL), evidence briefs co-produced with USAID, FIGO, and ICM, an interactive web-based guideline platform, HRP News, and the OptimizeMNH database.

sections.title: Chapter 6. Dissemination, applicability and updating of the guideline and recommendations

summary.text: Chapter 6, Sections 6.1 (continuation on local adaptation via the GREAT Network), 6.2 (Applicability issues and monitoring and evaluation), and 6.3 (Updating the guideline). Discusses anticipated implementation barriers (human resources, training, referral systems, equipment, commodities, and health management information systems), recommends clinical audits and interrupted time-series analyses to monitor coverage and quality of the 8-contact ANC model, and describes WHO's 5-year living-guideline update strategy, a planned 2-year implementation survey, and upcoming guideline work on GDM, syphilis, and haemoglobinopathies.
